title: Hybrid In-Memory KV with Durable WAL Snapshot Persistence (MiniDb Pattern)

claims.assertion: Local embedded storage engines for agent sessions should combine in-memory hash index performance with single-file WAL and CRC32-checksummed generational snapshots to guarantee zero native dependencies and multi-process crash consistency

context: Agent daemon architectures requiring fast search indices, session checkpointing, and cross-process IPC often suffer from the binary installation friction and file-locking quirks of full SQLite or LevelDB native drivers.
distilled_learning: MiniDb implements an embedded document/KV store using pure JavaScript/Python: 1) In-memory hash index with secondary B-Tree/date indexing, 2) Append-only write-ahead log (WAL) for microsecond mutation commits, 3) Generational snapshot compaction that merges the WAL into a clean baseline file under an exclusive file lock, and 4) Multi-reader support where follower processes tail the WAL and replay mutations into their local memory caches without write locks.
